Statement 3 is correct: the TFFF is Brazil's US$125 billion fund launched at COP30. So '1 only' misses a true statement, and the options containing 2 are wrong.
82.tq: TFFF = India only an observer; MAC = UAE + Indonesia, COP27.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is correct: **MAC** is led by the **UAE and Indonesia**, launched at **COP27 (Sharm el-Sheikh, 2022)**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **India joined the TFFF as an observer** (**2026**), not a full member.
Statement 3 is correct: the **TFFF** is Brazil's **US$125 billion** forest fund launched at **COP30**.
xa: The TFFF pays for **standing tropical forests**.
⚠ **MAC** = UAE + Indonesia at **COP27**; **TFFF** = Brazil at **COP30**.
**COP30** (**Belém**) was the first COP in the **Amazon**.

82.s: Which of the following correctly describes the NDC Transport Initiative for Asia?
o: It is funded by Germany's International Climate Initiative and covers China, India and Vietnam.
It is managed by Brazil to pay for standing tropical forests.
It is led by the UAE and Indonesia to restore mangroves in Asia.

xs: The oil spill off **Qeshm Island** (**Iran**, **Strait of Hormuz**, Aug 2026) threatened the **Hara mangroves** — option **(1)**, a **UNESCO BR**.
**Rushikulya** (Odisha) is an **Olive Ridley** nesting beach; **Keoladeo** is on the **Montreux Record**; the **Cold Desert BR** is in **Lahaul-Spiti, HP**.
xa: **Kerala** is drafting an **Oil Spill Contingency Plan**.
**Trinidad and Tobago** declared a **national emergency** over an **offshore oil spill** (2024, PYQ).
**Cold Desert BR** = India's **13th** in the UNESCO World Network (**Sep 2025**).

82.s: The 58th Tiger Reserve of India is:
82.x: Madhav National Park in Shivpuri district of Madhya Pradesh became India’s 58th Tiger Reserve.
82.tq: Direct recall of a designation number and site.
xs: **Madhav National Park (Shivpuri, MP)** is India's **58th Tiger Reserve** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam** (NSTR) is the **largest** TR, and **Cold Desert** is a **Biosphere Reserve**, not a TR.
xa: **MP** has the most TRs (**9**).
TRs cover **84,488 sq km** (**~2.6%** of India), up from **9** reserves in **1973**.

82.s: Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve, located in Lahaul-Spiti, Himachal Pradesh, became India’s which Biosphere Reserve in the UNESCO World Network?
82.x: Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve became India’s 13th Biosphere Reserve in the UNESCO World Network in September 2025. India has 18 Biosphere Reserves in all.
82.tq: Separate the national total from the World Network sequence number.
xs: **Cold Desert BR** (Lahaul-Spiti, HP) became India's **13th** in the **UNESCO World Network** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**18** is the total of India's Biosphere Reserves, not the World Network count.
xa: ⚠ **13th** = UNESCO World Network BRs; **18** = all BRs in India.
It was added in **Sep 2025** at the **37th MAB ICC**, **Hangzhou**.
It is India's first **high-altitude cold-desert** UNESCO BR.

82.s: Cold Desert is recognised as India’s first:
82.x: Cold Desert is India’s first high-altitude cold-desert UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
82.tq: Distinguish the UNESCO designation from Ramsar, geo-heritage and tiger-reserve categories.
xs: **Cold Desert** is India's **first high-altitude cold-desert UNESCO Biosphere Reserve** — option **(1)**.
It is in **Lahaul-Spiti, HP**, and became India's **13th** BR in the **UNESCO World Network** in **Sep 2025** (37th MAB ICC, Hangzhou).
xa: ⚠ **13th** = UNESCO World Network BRs; **18** = all BRs in India.
**National Geo-Heritage Sites** are declared by the **GSI**: **Kalinjar Hill** (Banda, UP), **Erra Matti Dibbalu** (near Visakhapatnam).
**Glaw Lake** (Kamlang TR) is **Arunachal's first** Ramsar site and India's **101st**.

82.s: Sphaerotheca varshaabhu, recently reported from India, is best described as which one of the following?
o: A lynx spider from Papikonda National Park
A burrowing frog from the urban landscape of Karnataka
A freshwater flowering plant from Telangana
82.x: Sphaerotheca varshaabhu is a new burrowing frog reported from the urban landscape of Bengaluru, Karnataka.
82.tq: Use the exact species–taxon–location association to eliminate nearby biological distractors.
xs: **Sphaerotheca varshaabhu** is a new **burrowing frog** from the urban landscape of **Karnataka** (Bengaluru) — so option **(3)** is correct.
The lynx spider of Papikonda NP is **Hamataliwa papikonda**; the Rajasthan lizard is **Mesalina bishnoi**; the Telangana plant is **Ammannia telanganensis**.
xa: It is a PYQ species, like **Impatiens karuppusamyi**, a new **plant** described by the **BSI**.
Exam angle: "new species" questions match the name with its **taxon** (plant/frog/spider) and the body (**BSI/ZSI**).
⚠ **Hamataliwa papikonda** = spider in **AP**; **Ammannia telanganensis** = plant in **Telangana**.

82.s: Simonia lawbah is significant because it represents:
o: The first deep-sea skate discovered under the Deep Ocean Mission
India's first species of the Mesalina genus
The first wolf snake from Great Nicobar Island
India's first species of the Simonia genus
82.x: Simonia lawbah, a ray spider from Krem Lawbah cave in Meghalaya, is India's first recorded Simonia species.
82.tq: Focus on the genus-level distinction rather than the broader animal category.
xs: **Simonia lawbah** is **India's first species of the Simonia genus** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The first **Mesalina** in India is the lizard **Mesalina bishnoi**; the deep-sea skate is **Dipturus dhritiae**; the Great Nicobar wolf snake is **Lycodon irwini**.
xa: It is a **ray spider** (**ZSI**) from **Krem Lawbah cave, Meghalaya** (**Jul 2026**).
⚠ **Simonia lawbah** = first **Simonia** (spider); **Mesalina bishnoi** = first **Mesalina** (lizard).
**Hamataliwa papikonda**, another ZSI spider, is a **lynx spider** from **Papikonda NP, AP**.

82.s: Ammannia telanganensis is a freshwater flowering plant reported from:
o: Alpine meadows of Jammu and Kashmir
Ranga Reddy wetlands and Amrabad Tiger Reserve in Telangana
82.x: Ammannia telanganensis was reported from the Ranga Reddy wetlands and Amrabad Tiger Reserve in Telangana in August 2026.
82.tq: Use the habitat and State together to distinguish a plant discovery from aquatic and cave species.
xs: **Ammannia telanganensis** is a freshwater flowering plant from the **Ranga Reddy wetlands and Amrabad TR (Telangana)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Alpine meadows of **J&K** gave three **Conocephalus katydids**; **Krem Lawbah** gave **Simonia lawbah**; **Kavaratti** gave a **laophontid copepod**.
xa: It was reported in **Aug 2026**.
⚠ **Ammannia telanganensis** = plant in **Telangana**; **Hamataliwa papikonda** = spider in **AP**.
Five **Allographa** lichen-forming fungi were found in the **Western Ghats**.

82.s: Impatiens karuppusamyi, reported in the news, is a new species of which type, and which body described it?
o: A burrowing frog described by the Zoological Survey of India
A plant described by the Botanical Survey of India
A lynx spider described by the Zoological Survey of India
A lichen-forming fungus described by the Botanical Survey of India
82.x: Impatiens karuppusamyi is a new plant species described by the Botanical Survey of India (asked 2024). The burrowing frog is Sphaerotheca varshaabhu, the lynx spider is Hamataliwa papikonda (ZSI), and the lichen-forming fungi are the five Allographa species of the Western Ghats.
82.tq: Plants -> BSI; animals -> ZSI.
xs: **Impatiens karuppusamyi** is a new **plant** described by the **Botanical Survey of India** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The burrowing frog is **Sphaerotheca varshaabhu**; the ZSI lynx spider is **Hamataliwa papikonda**; the lichen-forming fungi are five **Allographa** species.
xa: It was asked in a PYQ (**2024**).
Flora added in 2025: **353** taxa, **221** new to science.
Most new plants in 2025: **Arunachal Pradesh (49)**.

82.s: Which species were uplisted to Endangered in the earlier IUCN update of April 2026?
o: Emperor penguin and Antarctic fur seal
Olive Ridley turtle and greater one-horned rhinoceros
82.x: The emperor penguin and Antarctic fur seal were uplisted to Endangered in the April 2026 update.
82.tq: Direct recall of a paired species-list update.
xs: The **Emperor penguin** and **Antarctic fur seal** were uplisted to **Endangered** in **Apr 2026** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **numbat** and **desert rain frog** changed in the later **IUCN Red List 2026-1** (**Jul 2026**).
xa: Numbat: **EN → NT** (downlisted).
Desert rain frog: **NT → VU** (uplisted).
**Olive Ridley** nesting beaches in Odisha are threatened by **coastal erosion**.

82.s: India’s first AI-based human-elephant conflict research centre has been established at:
82.x: India’s first AI-based human-elephant conflict research centre is located at Palamu Tiger Reserve in Jharkhand.
82.tq: Direct recall of institution and location.
xs: India's first **AI-based human-elephant conflict research centre** is at **Palamu TR, Jharkhand** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Kuno NP** is the Project Cheetah site; **Gahirmatha** hosts Olive Ridley nesting; **Kaziranga** is the rhino park.
xa: The **'Gaja Mitra'** scheme for human-elephant conflict was approved by the **Karnataka** Cabinet.
AP uses **Kumki** elephants: **6** at the **Musallamadugu** camp, Palamaner (Chittoor).
AP's Kumki camps saw a **70%** fall in human deaths.

82.s: The mass nesting or arribada of Olive Ridley turtles in Odisha is associated with:
82.x: Olive Ridley arribada occurs at Gahirmatha and Rushikulya in Odisha. Coastal erosion threatens these nesting beaches.
82.tq: Direct site-species association.
xs: The **Olive Ridley arribada** in Odisha is at **Gahirmatha and Rushikulya** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Keoladeo and Loktak** are on the **Montreux Record**; **Qeshm Island** and the **Hara** mangroves are in **Iran**; **Kamlang** and **Cold Desert** are a TR and a BR.
xa: The threat is **coastal erosion** of the nesting beaches (**Aug 2026**).
**Operation Olivia**: Indian Coast Guard protection of Olive Ridley mass nesting.
It promotes **Turtle Excluder Devices** in fishing nets.

82.s: The 'Gaja Mitra' scheme to address human-elephant conflict was approved by the Cabinet of which State?
82.x: The Gaja Mitra scheme for human-elephant conflict was approved by the Karnataka Cabinet (asked 2025). Jharkhand hosts India's first AI-based human-elephant conflict research centre at Palamu TR; Kerala and Odisha are not linked to Gaja Mitra.
82.tq: Gaja Mitra = Karnataka; AI elephant centre = Palamu, Jharkhand.
xs: The **'Gaja Mitra'** scheme was approved by the **Karnataka** Cabinet — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jharkhand** hosts the first **AI-based** human-elephant conflict centre (**Palamu TR**), not Gaja Mitra.
xa: It was asked in a PYQ (**2025**).
AP's **Kumki** elephants came **from Karnataka**.
AP has **Kumki** camps at **Musalimadugu** and **Guchimi**.

82.s: 'Operation Olivia', conducted by the Indian Coast Guard, is aimed at:
o: Rescuing fishermen during cyclones in the Bay of Bengal
Protecting the mass nesting of Olive Ridley turtles
Containing oil spills off the Odisha coast
Translocating cheetahs to Kuno National Park
82.x: Operation Olivia is the Indian Coast Guard's operation to protect Olive Ridley mass nesting, with Turtle Excluder Devices promoted in fishing nets. It is not a cyclone rescue, oil-spill or cheetah operation.
82.tq: Olivia -> Olive Ridley.
xs: **Operation Olivia** is the Indian Coast Guard's operation to **protect Olive Ridley mass nesting** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is not a cyclone-rescue, oil-spill or cheetah operation.
xa: It also promotes **Turtle Excluder Devices** in nets.
Arribada sites: **Gahirmatha and Rushikulya (Odisha)**.
⚠ Do not confuse it with **Operation Sagar Bandhu**, India's response to Cyclone **Ditwah** in **Sri Lanka**.

82.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, which received UK CBAM recognition, is run by:
82.x: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is run by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency and received UK CBAM recognition.
82.tq: Use the implementing-body trap in which a ministry or regulator is substituted for the actual bureau.
xs: The **CCTS** is run by the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE)** — option **(3)**; it got **UK CBAM recognition** (Sep 2026).
**NTCA** manages **tiger reserves**, and the **Geological Survey of India** declares **National Geo-Heritage Sites**.
xa: **BEE** (Ministry of Power) with **AEEE** prepares the **State Energy Efficiency Index**: **AP** top in **2024**.
AP's SEEI score rose to **87.25** from **83.25**.
⚠ The **Green Credit Programme** (2023) credits are **non-tradable**.

82.s: Which country was identified as the most polluted country in the World Air Quality Report 2025?
82.x: Pakistan was identified as the most polluted country in the World Air Quality Report 2025.
82.tq: Use direct country-result recall while distinguishing country rankings from city rankings.
xs: **Pakistan** was the **most polluted country** in the **World Air Quality Report 2025** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**India** ranked **6th**, improving from **5th** in **2024**.
xa: Most polluted city: **Loni (UP)**; **New Delhi** was again the most polluted capital.
The report is by **IQAir, Switzerland** (**Mar 2026**).
In the **2024** edition, **Byrnihat (Meghalaya)** was the most polluted city.

82.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the World Air Quality Report 2025:
1. Loni in Uttar Pradesh was identified as the most polluted city.
2. India stood sixth, improving from fifth position in 2024.
3. New Delhi was identified as the most polluted capital.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: All three statements are correct. Loni was the most polluted city, India ranked sixth, and New Delhi was again the most polluted capital.
82.tq: Split the options by separating city, country and capital results.
xs: All three statements are correct, so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
Statement 1: **Loni (UP)** was the **most polluted city** in the **World Air Quality Report 2025** (**IQAir, Switzerland**, Mar 2026).
Statement 2: **India ranked 6th**, an improvement from **5th in 2024**.
Statement 3: **New Delhi** was again the **most polluted capital**; **Pakistan** was the most polluted country.
xa: The report is published by **IQAir**, a **Swiss** body; only **14%** of cities met the WHO PM2.5 guideline of **5 µg/m³**.
⚠ Most polluted city: **2024 = Byrnihat (Meghalaya)**; **2025 = Loni (UP)**.
⚠ Sources differ on how many years in a row Delhi has been the most polluted capital: **Drishti IAS** says the **8th** straight year; **RAU's IAS** implies the **7th**.
**Delhi** is the city most often in the news for poor air (asked 2025).

82.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. BASIC comprises Brazil, South Africa, India and China.
2. The Loss and Damage Fund was operationalised at COP29 in Baku.
3. Bhutan, Suriname and Panama are carbon-negative countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
82.x: Statement 1 is correct: BASIC = Brazil, South Africa, India, China. Statement 2 is wrong: the Loss and Damage Fund was operationalised at COP28 (Dubai); COP29 at Baku is known for the US$300 bn NCQG. Statement 3 is correct: Bhutan, Suriname and Panama are carbon-negative. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 2 are wrong.
82.tq: Loss and Damage Fund operationalised at COP28, Dubai.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **BASIC** = **Brazil, South Africa, India and China**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **Loss and Damage Fund** was operationalised at **COP28 (Dubai)**; **COP29 Baku** is known for the **US$300 bn NCQG**.
Statement 3 correct: **Bhutan, Suriname and Panama** are **carbon-negative** countries.
xa: **COP28** also gave the **Global Stocktake** and the call to **transition away from fossil fuels**.
India's long-term goal is **net zero by 2070**.
⚠ **US$300 bn** = NCQG (COP29); **US$1.3 trn** = Baku-Belém Roadmap (COP30).

82.s: The State of emergency in August 2026 due to the Bald Range wildfire was declared in:
82.x: The Bald Range wildfire occurred in British Columbia, Canada, where a state of emergency was declared and more than 20,000 people were evacuated.
82.tq: Direct country-event association.
xs: The **Bald Range wildfire** (Aug 2026) was in **British Columbia, Canada**, which declared a **state of emergency** — option **(4)**.
**20,000+** people were evacuated.
**Nepal** had flash floods, **Iran** an oil spill off **Qeshm Island**, and **Sri Lanka** was hit by **Cyclone Ditwah**.
xa: **Trinidad and Tobago** (PYQ) declared a **national emergency** over an **offshore oil spill** (2024).
**Nepal** floods (Bhotekoshi-Trishuli, 26 Aug 2026): toll **1,259**; **13 hydropower projects** damaged.
The Qeshm spill threatened the **Hara mangroves** (UNESCO BR).

82.s: Which country declared a national emergency in 2024 over an offshore oil spill?
82.x: Trinidad and Tobago declared a national emergency over an offshore oil spill in 2024 (PYQ). Iran's Qeshm Island oil spill was in Aug 2026, threatening the Hara mangroves; Sri Lanka is linked to Cyclone Ditwah. Mauritius is not linked to this event.
82.tq: 2024 oil-spill emergency = Trinidad and Tobago.
xs: **Trinidad and Tobago** declared a **national emergency** over an **offshore oil spill** in **2024** — option **(1)** (PYQ).
**Iran**'s spill off **Qeshm Island** came in **Aug 2026**; **Sri Lanka** is linked to **Cyclone Ditwah**, not an oil spill.
xa: The Qeshm Island spill (**Strait of Hormuz**) threatened the **Hara mangroves**, a UNESCO BR.
**Kerala** is drafting an **Oil Spill Contingency Plan**.
**Canada** (British Columbia) declared a **state of emergency** over the **Bald Range wildfire** (Aug 2026); **20,000+** evacuated.
**Nepal**'s Bhotekoshi-Trishuli flash floods (**26 Aug 2026**) killed **1,259**.

82.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the World Air Quality Report?
82.x: Byrnihat in Meghalaya was identified as the most polluted city in the World Air Quality Report 2024. Loni was the corresponding city in 2025.
82.tq: Use the edition-year distinction to avoid swapping successive report findings.
xs: **2024 — Byrnihat, Meghalaya** is correct — option **(3)**.
In **2025** the most polluted city was **Loni (UP)**, so options (1) and (2) swap the years.
**Rourkela** is a **Swachh Vayu 2026** category winner, not a polluted-city title.
xa: The report is by **IQAir, Switzerland**.
**2025**: **Pakistan** most polluted country (**13x** WHO limit); India **6th** (from **5th**).
Only **14%** of cities met the WHO PM2.5 guideline (**5 µg/m³**).

89.s:
Match List-I (Index / report) with List-II (Released by):
List-I
a. Global Talent Competitiveness Index
b. Rule of Law Index
c. World Economic Situation and Prospects 2026
d. World Inequality Report 2026
List-II
i. UN DESA
ii. INSEAD
iii. World Inequality Lab
iv. World Justice Project
Select the correct code:
89.x: The Global Talent Competitiveness Index is by INSEAD (a-ii); the Rule of Law Index by the World Justice Project (b-iv); the World Economic Situation and Prospects 2026 by UN DESA, New York (c-i); the World Inequality Report 2026 by the World Inequality Lab (d-iii). Option B swaps the Rule of Law Index and UN DESA; option C swaps INSEAD and the World Inequality Lab; option D mismatches all four.
89.tq: Pair each 'Lab', 'Project' and 'Institute' with the report named after it; INSEAD = talent.
xs: Correct match: **a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii** — option **(1)**.
**Global Talent Competitiveness Index** — **INSEAD**; **Rule of Law Index** — **World Justice Project**.
**World Economic Situation and Prospects 2026** — **UN DESA** (New York); **World Inequality Report 2026** — **World Inequality Lab**.
xa: **V-Dem Democracy Report** — **V-Dem Institute, University of Gothenburg**.
**International Migration Outlook 2025** — **OECD**; **Asia Power Index 2025** — Lowy Institute.
⚠ **Gender Gap** = **WEF**; **Gender Inequality Index** = **UNDP**.
⚠ **World Risk Index** = UNU-EHS; **Climate Risk Index** = Germanwatch.

89.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
89.x: The Global Wage Report is released by the International Labour Organization, not UNCTAD. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
89.tq: Find the swapped releasing agency among closely related reports.
xs: **Global Wage Report — UNCTAD** is the wrong pair — option **(1)**; the Global Wage Report is by the **ILO**.
The **ILO** also publishes the **World Social Protection Report** and **Employment and Social Trends 2026**, so options (2), (3) and (4) are correct.
xa: **UNCTAD** publishes the **World Investment Report**, **Digital Economy Report** and **Global Investment Trends Monitor**.
UNCTAD reported FDI into India up **73% to $47 bn** in **2025**.
**World Economic Situation and Prospects 2026** = **UN DESA** (New York).

89.s: The Human Development Index and the Gender Inequality Index are associated with which organisation?
o: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs
United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
89.x: UNDP releases both the Human Development Index and the Gender Inequality Index.
89.tq: Direct organisation–index association.
xs: Both the **HDI** and the **Gender Inequality Index** come from **UNDP (United Nations Development Programme)** — option **(2)**.
**UN DESA** releases the **World Economic Situation and Prospects**; **UNCTAD** the **World Investment Report**.
The **WEF** releases the **Global Gender Gap** Index — a different gender index.
xa: ⚠ **Gender Gap** = **WEF**; **Gender Inequality Index** = **UNDP**.
The **HDR** has appeared **since 1990**; the HDI was conceived by **Mahbub ul Haq** with **Amartya Sen**.
India: **HDI 130th of 193** (HDR 2025); **GII 108th** (2022 data).
The **Multidimensional Poverty Index** is by **UNDP + OPHI**.

89.s: The World Competitiveness Ranking is released by which institution?
89.x: The World Competitiveness Ranking is released by IMD in Lausanne.
89.tq: Discriminate between the IMD ranking and the WEF competitiveness report.
xs: The **World Competitiveness Ranking** is released by **IMD, Lausanne** — option **(1)**.
The **WEF** publishes the **Global Competitiveness Report / Index** — a different ranking.
The **OECD** publishes the **International Migration Outlook 2025**.
xa: **Global Talent Competitiveness Index** = **INSEAD**.
⚠ The notes do not give India's latest IMD rank.
WEF also issues the **Global Gender Gap**, the **Global Risks Report 2026** and the **Travel and Tourism (now Development) Index**.

89.s: Which of the following reports is NOT released by the World Bank?
89.x: The International Migration Outlook 2025 is released by the OECD. The Logistics Performance Index, Human Capital Index and Global Economic Prospects are associated with the World Bank.
89.tq: Find the one report belonging to a different international organisation.
xs: **International Migration Outlook 2025** is by the **OECD**, not the World Bank — option **(2)**.
**Global Economic Prospects**, the **Human Capital Index** and the **LPI** are all **World Bank** reports.
xa: The World Bank also publishes the **World Development Report 2025**.
India in **LPI 2023**: **38th of 139** (PYQ; 44th in 2018).
**World Economic Situation and Prospects 2026** = **UN DESA** (New York).

89.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
89.x: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime publishes the World Drug Report. The Frontiers Report is published by UNEP.
89.tq: Use agency–report association and eliminate swapped international organisations.
xs: **World Drug Report — UNODC** is correct — option **(3)**.
The **Frontiers Report** is by **UNEP**, so options (1) and (2) swap the bodies.
**Crime in India** is by the **NCRB (MHA)**, not UNCTAD.
xa: ⚠ The notes give no 2025-26 editions of the World Drug Report or the Frontiers Report.
**NCRB** news: **late release** of its data (Aug 2026).
**UNCTAD** publishes the **World Investment Report**.

89.s:
With reference to the Global Hunger Index, consider the following statements:
1. India's 2025 score was 25.8, in the 'serious' category.
2. In the 2024 edition, India ranked 111th of 125 countries.
3. In the 2025 edition, India ranked 102nd of 123 countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: GHI 2025 placed India 102nd of 123 with a score of 25.8 ('serious'). Statement 2 is wrong: in 2024 India was 105th of 127 (score 27.3); 111th of 125 was the 2023 edition. So option B; options A, C and D either leave out a correct statement or include the wrong one.
89.tq: GHI ranks: 2023 = 111/125, 2024 = 105/127, 2025 = 102/123 — rank and total both shrink.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
GHI **2025**: India **102nd of 123**, score **25.8**, "**serious**".
Statement 2 is wrong: in **2024** India was **105/127** (**27.3**); **111th of 125** was the **2023** edition.
xa: Publisher: **Concern Worldwide** + **Welthungerhilfe**.
⚠ GHI weights: undernourishment and under-5 mortality **1/3** each; stunting and wasting **1/6** each.
GHI uses **4** indicators on a **0-100** scale.

89.s: India's rank in the Global Innovation Index improved from 81 in 2015 and 48 in 2020 to which position in 2025?
89.x: India ranked 38th out of 139 economies in the Global Innovation Index 2025, improving from 81st in 2015 and 48th in 2020.
89.tq: Read a multi-year rank trend from the earliest to the latest edition.
xs: India was **38th of 139** in the **Global Innovation Index 2025** — option **(1)**.
xa: The GII is by **WIPO**; **NITI Aayog** is India's nodal agency.
**GII 2025** top: **Switzerland**, Sweden, USA; **China 10th**.
⚠ **GII** here = **Global Innovation Index**, not UNDP's **Gender Inequality Index**.

89.s: India's rank in the Gender Inequality Index based on 2022 data, reported in HDR 2023-24, was:
89.x: India ranked 108th in the Gender Inequality Index based on 2022 data.
89.tq: Avoid confusing the Gender Inequality Index with the HDI and other gender-related indices.
xs: India was **108th** in the **Gender Inequality Index 2022** (UNDP HDR 2023-24) — option **(3)** (PYQ fact).
**130th** is India's **HDI** rank; **91st** its **CPI 2025** rank; **118th** its **Happiness 2025** rank.
xa: ⚠ **Gender Inequality Index** = **UNDP**; **Gender Gap Index** = **WEF** (India **131st** in 2026).
⚠ "GII" in ranking tables usually means WIPO's **Global Innovation Index** (India **38th**).

89.s: Which of the following correctly represents India's V-Dem 2026 position?
o: 157th of 180, classified as a closed autocracy
127th of 163, classified as an electoral democracy
106th of 179, classified as an electoral autocracy
106th of 193, classified as a liberal democracy
89.x: India ranked 106th of 179 in the Electoral Democracy Index and was classified as an electoral autocracy.
89.tq: Match the index, total number of countries and classification as one unit.
xs: **V-Dem 2026**: India **106th of 179** (Electoral Democracy Index), an "**electoral autocracy**" — option **(3)**.
**157th of 180** is India's **Press Freedom** rank; **127th of 163** its **GPI** rank.
xa: India's score is the **lowest since 1975**.
V-Dem is by the **V-Dem Institute, University of Gothenburg** (Sweden).
India contests it: **V-Dem relies on expert opinion**.

89.s: Which State had the lowest score in the SDG India Index 2023–24?
89.x: Bihar had the lowest score, 57, in the SDG India Index 2023–24.
89.tq: Identify the bottom performer against the two top-performing States.
xs: **Bihar** had the lowest score (**57**) in the **SDG India Index 2023-24** — option **(2)**.
**Kerala** and **Uttarakhand** were top with **79**; **AP** was in the **top 10**.
xa: India's overall score: **71**.
The index is by **NITI Aayog** (**4th edition**, July 2024).
AP is **1st in SDG 7** and **2nd in SDG 14**.

89.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the latest releases and associated Indian positions mentioned for 2026?
o: Global Gender Gap 2026 placed India 176th, while V-Dem 2026 placed India 131st.
Global Gender Gap 2026 placed India 131st, while V-Dem 2026 placed India 176th.
Global Gender Gap 2026 placed India 106th, while V-Dem 2026 placed India 131st.
Global Gender Gap 2026 placed India 131st, while V-Dem 2026 placed India 106th.
89.x: Global Gender Gap 2026 placed India 131st, and V-Dem 2026 placed India 106th. The Global Gender Gap release was identified as dated 17 September 2026.
89.tq: Separate similarly timed indices by their rank figures.
xs: **Global Gender Gap 2026** placed India **131st**; **V-Dem 2026** placed India **106th** — option **(4)**.
**176th** is India's **EPI 2026** rank, the third of the newest releases.
xa: The Gender Gap 2026 was released on **17 Sep 2026** by the **WEF**.
V-Dem: **106th of 179**, "**electoral autocracy**"; score lowest since **1975**.
EPI 2026 (Yale + Columbia): **176th of 177**, score **22.46**.

89.s: The Human Development Index, published by UNDP in its Human Development Report since 1990, was conceived by:
o: Mahbub ul Haq, with Amartya Sen
89.x: The HDI was conceived by Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq, working with Amartya Sen; UNDP has published the HDR since 1990. Sen contributed but was not the sole originator. Stiglitz and Bhagwati are not linked to the HDI.
89.tq: HDI: Mahbub ul Haq (with Sen), UNDP, 1990.
xs: The **HDI** was conceived by **Mahbub ul Haq, with Amartya Sen** — option **(2)**.
So Sen worked **with** Haq: he was not the sole originator.
**UNDP** has published the **HDR since 1990**.
xa: HDI uses **GNI per capita (PPP)** and combines dimensions with a **geometric mean**.
**HDR 2025** theme: "**A Matter of Choice: People and Possibilities in the Age of AI**".
India: **130 of 193**, HDI **0.685** (from 0.676), **Medium** category.
⚠ UNDP's **Gender Inequality Index** (India **108th**) differs from the WEF's **Gender Gap** (India **131st**).

89.s: Which of the following correctly describes the weights used in the Global Hunger Index?
o: Undernourishment 1/3, child stunting 1/3, child wasting 1/6, under-five mortality 1/6
Undernourishment 1/3, child stunting 1/6, child wasting 1/6, under-five mortality 1/3
Undernourishment 1/4, child stunting 1/4, child wasting 1/4, under-five mortality 1/4
Undernourishment 1/6, child stunting 1/3, child wasting 1/3, under-five mortality 1/6
89.x: The Global Hunger Index assigns one-third each to undernourishment and under-five mortality, and one-sixth each to child stunting and child wasting.
89.tq: Compare fractional weights carefully and identify the two equally weighted major components.
xs: **GHI** weights: **undernourishment 1/3**, **under-5 mortality 1/3**, **child stunting 1/6**, **child wasting 1/6** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) wrongly gives stunting **1/3** and mortality **1/6**; the GHI has **4 indicators** on a **0-100** scale.
xa: ⚠ GHI weights: **1/3 + 1/3** (undernourishment, under-5 mortality) and **1/6 + 1/6** (stunting, wasting).
The GHI is by **Concern Worldwide + Welthungerhilfe**.

89.s:
With reference to the Human Development Index (UNDP), consider the following statements:
1. It uses GNI per capita (PPP) as its income measure.
2. Its dimension indices are combined using an arithmetic mean.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: the HDI uses GNI per capita (PPP). Statement 2 is wrong: the HDI combines its dimension indices using a geometric mean, not an arithmetic mean. So 1 only.
89.tq: HDI = GNI per capita (PPP) + geometric mean.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **HDI** uses **GNI per capita (PPP)**.
Statement 2 wrong: it uses a **geometric mean**, not an arithmetic mean.
xa: The HDI is by **UNDP** (**HDR since 1990**), conceived by **Mahbub ul Haq** with **Amartya Sen**.
India in **HDR 2025**: **130 of 193**, HDI **0.685**, **Medium** category.
**HDR 2021-22** top: **Switzerland**.

89.s: Which statement about PGI 2.0 2025–26 is correct?
o: A state attained the top Utkarsh grade and Meghalaya was highest.
No state reached the top Utkarsh grade, Chandigarh first reached Uttam-3, and Meghalaya was lowest.
Chandigarh was placed in the Utkarsh grade and Tamil Nadu was lowest.
Meghalaya first reached Uttam-3 and Chandigarh was lowest.
89.x: No state reached the top Utkarsh grade; Chandigarh became the first to reach Uttam-3, while Meghalaya was the lowest performer.
89.tq: Combine an exception, a first achievement and the lowest performer in one statement set.
xs: **PGI 2.0 2025-26**: **no state** reached the top **'Utkarsh'** grade; **Chandigarh** first reached **'Uttam-3'**; **Meghalaya** was lowest — option **(2)**.
Options (1), (3) and (4) reverse Chandigarh and Meghalaya or invent an Utkarsh state.
xa: PGI 2.0 was released by the **Ministry of Education** (**Jul 2026**).
**LEADS 2025** (Ministry of Commerce) introduced a new **4-tier** grading.
**NIRF** (also Ministry of Education): **Tamil Nadu** has the most top-100 institutions (**17**).

89.s: According to the India Skills Report 2026, which group recorded higher employability for the first time in five years?
o: Women, at 54%, compared with men at 51.5%
Men, at 54%, compared with women at 51.5%
Women, at 51.5%, compared with men at 54%
89.x: Women’s employability was 54%, exceeding men’s 51.5% for the first time in five years.
89.tq: Check both the direction of comparison and the associated percentages.
xs: Employability of **women (54%)** exceeded that of **men** (**51.5%**) for the **first time in 5 years** — option **(1)**.
Option (4) swaps the two figures.
xa: The **India Skills Report** is by **Wheebox** and partners.
**ISR 2024** (asked): top talent states = **Maharashtra, UP, Kerala**.
**QS Future Skills Index 2027**: India **13th**, **1st** among lower-middle-income economies.

89.s: According to the India Skills Report 2024, which States were the top destinations for talent?
89.x: The India Skills Report 2024 named Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Kerala as the top talent States (asked in the exam). The other combinations are incorrect.
89.tq: ISR 2024 talent: Maharashtra-UP-Kerala.
xs: **ISR 2024** top talent states: **Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Kerala** — option **(2)** (asked in the exam).
The other combinations do not match the notes' list of top talent states.
xa: **ISR 2026**: women's employability **54%** above men's **51.5%**.
⚠ **Maharashtra** also tops the **Export Preparedness Index 2024**.
**Tamil Nadu** has the most **NIRF 2025** top-100 institutions (**17**).

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the SDG India Index 2023-24:
1. It is the fourth edition, released by NITI Aayog in July 2024.
2. Kerala and Uttarakhand topped it with a score of 79.
3. Andhra Pradesh ranked first in SDG 14 and second in SDG 7.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: NITI Aayog released the 4th edition in July 2024 (India's score 71). Statement 2 is correct: Kerala and Uttarakhand topped with 79 (Bihar lowest, 57). Statement 3 is wrong: AP was 1st in SDG 7 (energy) and 2nd in SDG 14, not the reverse. So options with 3 are wrong.
89.tq: AP: 1st in SDG 7, 2nd in SDG 14 - watch for the swap.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **4th edition**, released by **NITI Aayog** in **July 2024**.
Statement 2 correct: **Kerala** and **Uttarakhand** topped with **79**.
Statement 3 wrong: AP was **1st in SDG 7** and **2nd in SDG 14** — the reverse of the statement.
xa: India's score **71**; **Bihar (57)** bottom.
**AP in top 10**; but AP slipped in **SDG 9** (13→21), **SDG 5** (5→14) and **SDG 8** (6→16).
⚠ UN SDSN's **SDG Index 2025**: India **99th of 167**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026:
1. Lucknow topped its category.
2. Rourkela topped its category.
3. Kalinga Nagar topped its category.
4. Guntur jointly secured second position in the 3–10 lakh population category.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: All four statements are correct. Lucknow, Rourkela and Kalinga Nagar topped their respective categories, while Guntur was joint second in the 3–10 lakh category.
89.tq: Check category-wise ranking statements and the population-range detail.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Lucknow**, **Rourkela** and **Kalinga Nagar** topped their categories in **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026**.
**Guntur** was **joint 2nd** in the **3-10 lakh** category.
xa: Swachh Vayu covers the **130 NCAP cities**.
⚠ **Swachh Survekshan** (cleanliness, QCI) = **Indore**; **Swachh Vayu** (air) = Lucknow / Rourkela / Kalinga Nagar.
Other AP ranks: **MISHTI 2nd**; **rooftop solar 5th** (some notes say **4th**).

89.s: Under the new Super Swachh League of Swachh Survekshan 2024–25, which city ranked first in the 10 lakh-plus category?
89.x: Indore ranked first in the 10 lakh-plus category and achieved the distinction for the eighth time. Surat and Navi Mumbai followed it.
89.tq: Match the category winner with the correct city and achievement count.
xs: **Indore** topped the new **Super Swachh League** (**10 lakh+**) of **Swachh Survekshan 2024-25**, for the **8th** time — option **(1)**.
**Surat** and **Navi Mumbai** followed.
xa: Swachh Survekshan is a **MoHUA** survey, conducted by the **QCI**.
It started in **2016** with **73** cities; **4,589** cities surveyed in 2024-25.
⚠ Do not confuse it with **Swachh Vayu** (air): **Lucknow** tops the million-plus category.

89.s: Swachh Survekshan 2024-25 is conducted by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs with the survey being run by:
o: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
89.x: Swachh Survekshan is conducted under MoHUA and the survey is run by the Quality Council of India.
89.tq: Identify the implementing body rather than the parent ministry.
xs: **Swachh Survekshan 2024-25** is a **MoHUA** survey run by the **Quality Council of India (QCI)** — option **(3)**.
**BEE** runs the **State Energy Efficiency Index**; **MoEFCC** runs **NCAP**.
xa: Started in **2016** with **73** cities; **4,589** cities in 2024-25.
**Super Swachh League** (10 lakh+): **Indore** → Surat → Navi Mumbai.
⚠ **Swachh Vayu** covers the **130 NCAP cities**.

89.s: Which State ranked first among 19 large and medium States in consumer justice delivery according to the India Justice Report Consumer Justice Report 2026?
89.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked first among 19 large and medium States in consumer justice delivery. Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Karnataka and West Bengal followed it.
89.tq: Read the ranking order from the first position rather than selecting a familiar State.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** ranked **1st** among **19** large/mid States in the **IJR Consumer Justice Report 2026** — option **(3)**.
**MP, Rajasthan, Karnataka and West Bengal** followed.
xa: It was released in **Mar 2026**.
⚠ **IJR 2025** = AP **2nd**; **IJR Consumer Justice 2026** = AP **1st**.
The IJR is supported by **Tata Trusts** (first in **2019**).

89.s: In the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index 2023 (the latest edition), India's rank was:
89.x: India ranked 38th of 139 in LPI 2023, up from 44th in 2018 (PYQ). 44th was the 2018 position; 54th and 22nd are not India's LPI ranks. Note that India's GII 2025 rank is also 38/139, but that index is by WIPO, not the World Bank.
89.tq: LPI 2023 and GII 2025: both 38/139 - don't mix the publishers (World Bank vs WIPO).
xs: India was **38th of 139** in **LPI 2023** (latest) — option **(2)**, a **PYQ** fact.
**44th** was India's **2018** rank.
xa: The **LPI** is a **World Bank** index.
⚠ **38th of 139** is also India's **GII 2025** rank, but the GII is by **WIPO**.
The World Bank also publishes the **Human Capital Index** and **Global Economic Prospects**.

89.s: Which of the following criticisms is associated with the V-Dem and Environmental Performance indices respectively?
o: V-Dem relies on expert opinion, while EPI ignores per-capita emissions.
V-Dem ignores expert opinion, while EPI uses only per-capita emissions.
Both indices rely exclusively on government data.
89.x: V-Dem is criticised because it relies on expert opinion, while the EPI is criticised for ignoring per-capita emissions.
89.tq: Match each criticism with the correct index.
xs: **V-Dem relies on expert opinion**, while the **EPI ignores per-capita emissions** — option **(1)**.
These are India's reasons for **contesting perception-based indices**.
xa: Data gaps: **GII 2024** had missing data for **two** indicators and outdated data for **eight**.
The government dismisses **Press Freedom** ranks as **biased**.
V-Dem is by the **V-Dem Institute, University of Gothenburg** (Sweden); EPI by **Yale + Columbia**.

89.s: Which country ranked first in Doing Business 2020?
89.x: New Zealand ranked first in Doing Business 2020.
89.tq: Distinguish the Doing Business leader from leaders of other global indices.
xs: **New Zealand** ranked **1st** in **Doing Business 2020** — option **(3)**.
**Denmark** tops the **CPI**; **Switzerland** tops the **GII 2025**; **Singapore** is 3rd in **CPI 2025** and **NRI 2025**.
xa: **Switzerland** also topped **HDR 2021-22**.
**NRI 2025** top: **USA, Finland, Singapore**.
**New Zealand** is **2nd** in the **GPI 2026**, after Iceland.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about the Padma awards:
1. The Padma Vibhushan is given for exceptional and distinguished service and is India's second-highest civilian award.
2. The Padma Bhushan is given for distinguished service in any field and is India's fourth-highest civilian award.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: Padma Vibhushan = exceptional and distinguished service, 2nd highest. Statement 2 is wrong: Padma Bhushan is for distinguished service of a high order and is 3rd highest; 'distinguished service in any field' and 4th place describe the Padma Shri. So only 1 is correct; 2 only, both and neither are wrong.
96.tq: Vibhushan = exceptional (2nd), Bhushan = high order (3rd), Shri = any field (4th).
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Padma Vibhushan** is for **exceptional and distinguished service** and is the **2nd highest** civilian award.
Statement 2 wrong: the **Padma Bhushan** is for **distinguished service of high order** and ranks **3rd**; "any field" and **4th** describe the **Padma Shri**.
xa: The **Bharat Ratna** was last given in **2024** (**5** awardees, incl. **P.V. Narasimha Rao**).
Padma awards were instituted in **1954**; announced on **Republic Day**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about the Padma awards:
1. They were instituted in 1954.
2. They are announced every year on Independence Day.
3. They are conferred by the President at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Padma awards were instituted in 1954. Statement 2 is wrong: they are announced on Republic Day, not Independence Day. Statement 3 is correct: the President confers them at Rashtrapati Bhavan (around March-April). Hence 1 and 3 only; any option containing 2 is wrong, and '1 only' misses statement 3.
96.tq: Padma = Republic Day announcement, President confers, since 1954.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(4) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the Padma awards were **instituted in 1954**.
Statement 2 wrong: they are announced on **Republic Day**, not Independence Day.
Statement 3 correct: the **President** confers them at **Rashtrapati Bhavan** (around March-April).
xa: ⚠ **1954** = Padma awards instituted + **Sahitya Akademi** inaugurated.
2026 awards were presented in **two investitures**, the second at **Ganatantra Mandap**, Rashtrapati Bhavan.
Legal status: **not "titles" under Art. 18** (**Balaji Raghavan case, 1996**).

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional status of the Padma awards:
1. They are not titles prohibited by Article 18 of the Constitution.
2. Article 18 expressly bars military and academic distinctions.
3. They may be used as prefixes or suffixes to a recipient’s name.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Balaji Raghavan case (1996) held that Padma awards are not 'titles' under Article 18. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 18 exempts military and academic distinctions rather than barring them. Statement 3 is wrong: the awards cannot be used as prefixes or suffixes. So 1 only.
96.tq: Watch for the reversed constitutional exception and the false claim about use as a title.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Balaji Raghavan case (1996)** held that Padma awards are **not "titles" under Art. 18**.
Statement 2 wrong: **Art. 18** **exempts** military and academic distinctions; it does not bar them.
Statement 3 wrong: the awards **cannot be used as prefix or suffix**.
xa: The same rule applies to the **Bharat Ratna**.
**Padma Vibhushan** is the **2nd highest** civilian award; **Padma Bhushan** 3rd; **Padma Shri** 4th.
AP demanded the Bharat Ratna for **NTR** (Feb 2026).

96.s: In which case was it held that national civilian awards such as the Padma awards are not titles under Article 18?
96.x: The Balaji Raghavan case of 1996 dealt with the status of national awards under Article 18.
96.tq: Match the constitutional issue with the case specifically associated with it.
xs: The **Balaji Raghavan case (1996)** held that national awards are **not "titles" under Art. 18** — option **(4)**.
Hence they cannot be used as a **prefix or suffix** to the name.
xa: **Art. 18** exempts **military and academic distinctions**.
The ruling covers both the **Padma awards** and the **Bharat Ratna**.
**Bharat Ratna** last given in **2024** to **5** awardees.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about the Padma Bhushan 2026:
1. Mammootty was recognised in the field of art.
2. Alka Yagnik was recognised in the field of art.
3. Vijay Amritraj was recognised in the field of sports.
4. Shibu Soren received the award posthumously for public affairs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: All four statements are correct: Mammootty and Alka Yagnik were recognised in art, Vijay Amritraj in sports, and Shibu Soren posthumously in public affairs.
96.tq: Check each person against the stated field and posthumous status before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Mammootty** and **Alka Yagnik**: **Padma Bhushan** for **art**.
**Vijay Amritraj**: **sports**; **Shibu Soren**: **posthumous**, **public affairs**.
xa: Other 2026 PB awardees: **Uday Kotak** (trade and industry) and oncologist **Dattatreyudu Nori**.
Padma Shri sports 2026: **Rohit Sharma**, **Harmanpreet Kaur**, **Savita Punia**.
Criticism: **South Indian** artists get national honours late or a lower grade of Padma.

96.s: The Padma awards announced on 25 January 2026 comprised:
o: 131 awards: 5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri
139 awards: 7 Padma Vibhushan, 19 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri
131 awards: 7 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 111 Padma Shri
113 awards: 5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 95 Padma Shri
96.x: The 2026 list had 131 awards: 5 PV, 13 PB, 113 PS. 139 awards with a 7/19/113 split was the 2025 list; the other splits do not match either year.
xs: The **2026** list had **131** awards: **5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan, 113 Padma Shri** — option **(1)**.
**139** with **7 / 19 / 113** was the **2025** list; the other splits match neither year.
xa: ⚠ Padma Shri = **113** in both **2025** and **2026**.
2025: **23** women and **9** posthumous awardees; one award to a **duo**.
2026 PV awardees include **V.S. Achuthanandan** and **Dharmendra** (both posthumous).

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 60th Jnanpith Award:
1. R. Vairamuthu was the third Tamil winner.
2. He was the first recipient honoured mainly for poetry.
3. The award was given posthumously.
4. The award carries ₹11 lakh and a bronze Saraswati statuette.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: R. Vairamuthu was the third Tamil winner and the first honoured mainly for poetry; the award carries ₹11 lakh and a bronze Saraswati. It was not posthumous.
96.tq: Locate the single reversed eligibility or status detail among otherwise precise statements.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 4 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **R. Vairamuthu** is the **3rd Tamil** winner.
Statement 2 correct: the **first** honoured mainly for **poetry**.
Statement 3 wrong: the award was **not posthumous**.
Statement 4 correct: the Jnanpith carries **₹11 lakh** and a **bronze Saraswati**.
xa: It was the **60th Jnanpith**, for **2025**, announced **Mar 2026**.
The Jnanpith was instituted in **1961** and first given in **1965**.
First **Telugu** winner: **Viswanatha Satyanarayana** (**1970**).

96.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025?
o: Sa. Tamilselvan — Jeete Jee Allahabad — Tamil
96.x: Navtej Sarna received the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 for the English novel Crimson Spring. Mamta Kalia was recognised for Jeete Jee Allahabad, and Sa. Tamilselvan for Tamil criticism.
96.tq: Match all three elements—recipient, work and language—to avoid partial-pair traps.
xs: **Navtej Sarna — Crimson Spring — English** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Mamta Kalia** won for **'Jeete Jee Allahabad'** (Hindi memoir); **Sa. Tamilselvan** for **Tamil criticism**.
**Heart Lamp** is **Banu Mushtaq**'s International Booker 2025 winner.
xa: Sahitya Akademi 2025 covered **24 languages**, announced **16 Mar 2026** after a **Culture Ministry hold**.
The award carries **₹1 lakh**.
Criticism: Sahitya Akademi awards were held back for "**restructuring**".

96.s: The Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 was given in
o: 24 languages, comprising only Eighth Schedule languages
22 languages, all from the Eighth Schedule
26 languages, including Hindi and Sanskrit only
24 languages, comprising 22 Eighth Schedule languages, English and Rajasthani
96.x: The 2025 Sahitya Akademi Awards covered 24 languages: 22 Eighth Schedule languages, English and Rajasthani.
96.tq: Separate the total number of languages from the constitutional-language component.
xs: Sahitya Akademi 2025 was given in **24 languages**: **22 Eighth Schedule** languages + **English** + **Rajasthani** — option **(4)**.
So it is not limited to Eighth Schedule languages: **English** and **Rajasthani** are the two extra.
xa: The award carries **₹1 lakh**.
The Akademi was founded in **1952**, inaugurated **12 Mar 1954**, registered as a society in **1956**.
2025 winners include **Navtej Sarna** ('Crimson Spring', English) and **Mamta Kalia** (Hindi).

96.s: The International Booker Prize 2025 was awarded for
o: Heart Lamp by Banu Mushtaq, translated by Deepa Bhasthi
The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny by Kiran Desai
96.x: Banu Mushtaq’s Kannada story collection Heart Lamp, translated by Deepa Bhasthi, won the International Booker Prize 2025.
96.tq: Match the year, work, author and translator while separating shortlisted works from winners.
xs: **International Booker 2025**: **'Heart Lamp'** by **Banu Mushtaq** (Kannada stories), translated by **Deepa Bhasthi** — option **(2)**.
**'Flesh'** (David Szalay) won the **Booker 2025**; **Taiwan Travelogue** won the **International Booker 2026**.
Kiran Desai's novel was only **shortlisted** for the Booker 2025.
xa: International Booker 2026 was the **first Mandarin Chinese** winner.
The International Booker prize is **£50,000**, split between **author and translator**.

96.s: Which one of the following was shortlisted for the Booker Prize 2025?
o: The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny by Kiran Desai
96.x: Kiran Desai’s The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny was shortlisted for the Booker Prize 2025; David Szalay’s Flesh was the winner.
96.tq: Distinguish the winner from a shortlisted title and from International Booker entries.
xs: **Kiran Desai's 'The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny'** was **shortlisted** for the **Booker 2025** — option **(3)**.
**'Flesh'** by **David Szalay** won it; **Heart Lamp** and **Taiwan Travelogue** are **International Booker** winners (2025 and 2026).
xa: ⚠ **Heart Lamp** = Banu Mushtaq (Intl Booker **2025**); **Taiwan Travelogue** = Yáng Shuāng-zǐ (**2026**).
Heart Lamp was translated by **Deepa Bhasthi**; Taiwan Travelogue by **Lin King**.

96.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a Telugu literary award fact?
o: Gurram Jashuva — Sahitya Akademi Award for Gabbilam
Viswanatha Satyanarayana — Sahitya Akademi Award for Viswambhara
Boyi Bhimanna — Sahitya Akademi Award for Gudisale Kalipotunnayi
Narayana Reddy — Jnanpith Award for Paakudu Raallu
96.x: Boyi Bhimanna received the Sahitya Akademi Award for Gudisale Kalipotunnayi. Gurram Jashuva was not awarded for Gabbilam; the other works belong to different recipients and awards.
96.tq: Find the correctly matched recipient–work pair among deliberately swapped literary works.
xs: **Boyi Bhimanna — Sahitya Akademi for Gudisale Kalipotunnayi** is correct — option **(3)**; he won it in **1975**.
**Gurram Jashuva** was **not** awarded for **Gabbilam**.
**Viswambhara** won **C. Narayana Reddy** the **Jnanpith (1988)**; **Paakudu Raallu** is **Ravuri Bharadwaja**'s Jnanpith work.
xa: Boyi Bhimanna also got the **Padma Shri** (**1973**; some notes say 1975) and **Padma Bhushan** (**2001**).
First Telugu Jnanpith: **Viswanatha Satyanarayana** (**1970**).
⚠ The notes do not name the **Telugu** winner of the Sahitya Akademi 2025.

96.s:

115.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to persons who died in 2025–2026?
1. Khaleda Zia — Bangladesh’s first woman Prime Minister and BNP leader
2. Mark Tully — Journalist and author
3. Madhav Gadgil — Ecologist associated with People’s Biodiversity Registers
4. T.K. Oommen — Sociologist and recipient of Padma Bhushan in 2008
115.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Khaleda Zia was Bangladesh’s first woman Prime Minister, Mark Tully was a journalist and author, Madhav Gadgil was an ecologist, and T.K. Oommen received the Padma Bhushan in 2008.
115.tq: Use a statement-based scan to verify each person against the associated field and distinction.
xs: All four pairs are correctly matched — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
**Khaleda Zia** — Bangladesh's **first woman PM** (BNP), died **Dec 2025** (aged **80**); **Mark Tully** — **journalist, author**, died **Jan 2026** (**90**).
**Madhav Gadgil** — ecologist (**People's Biodiversity Registers**, Western Ghats panel); **T.K. Oommen** — sociologist, **Padma Bhushan 2008**.
xa: ⚠ **K.N. Panikkar** and **Sumit Sarkar** = historians; **T.K. Oommen** = sociologist; **Habermas** = philosopher.
Gadgil was called the **"people's ecologist"**.

115.s: The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners is:
o: Five years or until the age of 62, whichever is earlier
Six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
Five years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
Six years without an age limit
115.x: The CEC and Election Commissioners hold office for six years or until age 65, whichever is earlier. Five years and age 62 are traps, and there is an age limit.
115.tq: Check both components of a tenure rule: duration and age limit.
xs: The **CEC** and Election Commissioners serve **6 years or till age 65**, whichever is earlier — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Five years** and **age 62** are traps; there is an age limit.
xa: Present **CEC**: **Gyanesh Kumar**.
The SC said the **CJI**'s place on the selection panel (**Anoop Baranwal**, **Mar 2023**) was **temporary** (May 2026).
